- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing filter to dampen immediate post-spike peaks.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, adjust downward by 2–5% to align with historical mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3 consecutive +0.3+ sentiment), model tends to overforecast; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (±0.3), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add ±1–2% noise to forecast to reflect uncertainty.  
- Model underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is high but price is falling — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
